objective: Send a webhook notification when a todo is marked done via POST /todos/{id}/done, reusing the existing fire-and-forget webhook infra (app/webhooks.py), with customer webhook URL registration — without changing the frozen stage-1 API shape (C1) or breaking the done transition.
in_scope: webhook URL registration: additive optional webhook_url field on the todo record (C2 additive per its unfreeze rule) set at todo creation
done -> webhook dispatch: marking a todo done sends exactly one webhook to the registered URL with a deterministic payload, via the existing WebhookDispatcher
failure tolerance: webhook send failure (or missing URL) never breaks the done transition — POST /todos/{id}/done still returns 200 and the todo is done
tests: new notification suite + the frozen stage-1 suite stays green with the C1 response key set unchanged

out_of_scope.item: last_notified_at timestamp in the GET /todos response (product ticket note)
out_of_scope.reason: would change the frozen C1 api contract (stage 1, exact per-todo key set). C1's unfreeze rule allows change only via a formal contract change request with sign-off — a product ticket note is input to that request, not the request itself. The decision is recorded as open question Q1 with owner user; if approved, C1 is revised (request_contract_revision) and the field is planned as a follow-on stage. It is NOT absorbed into this stage.

out_of_scope.item: webhook retry, delivery history, or per-webhook management endpoints
out_of_scope.reason: the existing dispatcher is fire-and-forget by design; management surface is a separate future stage with its own contract work

frozen_assumptions.statement: the service runs single-process with the in-memory store; no persistence layer is involved
frozen_assumptions.rationale: carried over from stage 1 (verified there); store.py still holds everything in memory

frozen_assumptions.statement: WebhookDispatcher.send never raises: the fixture records and returns a status; the real deployment logs and swallows failures by design, so a send failure cannot propagate into the done transition
frozen_assumptions.rationale: app/webhooks.py docstring + README platform notes; if a deployment ever made send() raise, DA-2's try/except boundary still protects the transition

frozen_architecture.decision: TodoAPI is the only writer to the store; handlers never mutate store state directly

the webhook dispatch happens inside mark_done, strictly after the store mutation, through the existing WebhookDispatcher, wrapped so that any exception is caught and logged and never propagates to the caller
frozen_architecture.rationale: notification is best-effort per the task's hard requirement (failure must not break the done transition) and the infra's fire-and-forget design; no new worker/queue layer is introduced

shared_contracts.spec: GET /todos response: {todos: [{id: string, title: string, done: boolean, tag?: string}]} — exactly these keys per todo, in creation order; 400 {error} on malformed filter params
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: only via a contract change request with product sign-off; external clients depend on the exact key set

shared_contracts.spec: todo record shape in store: {id: 't<n>', title: string, done: boolean, tag?: string, webhook_url?: string}; creation order preserved. Stage-2 additive: webhook_url (optional string) added per C2's unfreeze rule (additive-only; stage 2 proposes it in writing in this contract). last_notified_at is intentionally NOT added — it ships only if/when C1 is revised (see Q1).
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: additive-only until stage 2 proposes otherwise in writing

shared_contracts.spec: done-notification contract: on a successful mark_done (todo exists, transition applied), exactly one webhook is dispatched to the todo's webhook_url with payload {event: 'todo.done', todo_id: string, title: string, at: ISO-8601 timestamp}; if webhook_url is absent, exactly zero dispatches. Dispatch never affects the HTTP result: POST /todos/{id}/done returns 200 {id, done: true} (404 for unknown id) regardless of dispatch outcome, and a dispatch exception is caught+logged, never raised
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: payload shape may grow additively in a later stage only via a contract change request

integration_seams.description: handler -> store boundary: every read/write goes through TodoStore methods
mark_done -> webhook dispatch boundary: the API handler calls WebhookDispatcher.send exactly once per successful transition, after the store mutation, inside a no-escape exception boundary

acceptance.description: marking a todo with a registered webhook_url done dispatches exactly one webhook with the C3 payload and returns 200
acceptance.positive_case: create todo with webhook_url='https://hooks.example/cb'; mark done -> WebhookLog.sent has exactly 1 entry {url: 'https://hooks.example/cb', payload: {event: 'todo.done', todo_id, title, at}} and response is 200 {id, done: true}
acceptance.negative_case: marking the same todo done again is a no-op state-wise but still returns 200 (idempotent transition)
acceptance.failure_behavior: if the dispatcher is replaced by one that raises, the response is still 200, the todo is done, and the exception is swallowed (asserted, not inferred)

acceptance.description: a todo without webhook_url is marked done with zero dispatches and status 200 (the test asserts an empty WebhookLog.sent)
acceptance.positive_case: create todo without webhook_url; mark done -> WebhookLog.sent stays empty, response status 200 {id, done: true}
acceptance.negative_case: no implicit default URL and no error status: the API returns 200 and the test asserts no 400 and no default dispatch
acceptance.failure_behavior: missing webhook_url is a valid record state, not an error: the API returns 200 and the test asserts no dispatch was logged

acceptance.description: the done transition survives a raising dispatcher (failure tolerance, hard requirement): the handler catches the exception and still returns 200
acceptance.positive_case: TodoAPI wired to a dispatcher whose send() raises RuntimeError; mark done -> response status 200, the store record shows done=true, no exception reaches the caller
acceptance.negative_case: no half-state: the store record is done=true even when the send failed (asserted, not inferred)
acceptance.failure_behavior: the exception raised by the dispatcher is caught at the DA-2 boundary, logged, and the transition is intact: response status stays 200

acceptance.description: the frozen C1 response shape is unchanged by stage 2 (no last_notified_at): the test asserts the exact per-todo key set
acceptance.positive_case: after stage-2 work, GET /todos per-todo keys are exactly {id, title, done} (+tag when set) — asserted by the unmodified stage-1 frozen suite test tests/test_api.py::test_create_and_list_shape
acceptance.negative_case: no last_notified_at key appears in any todo of the GET /todos response (the test asserts its absence)
acceptance.failure_behavior: an added key fails the frozen suite's exact-key-set assertion — the test suite is the canary

constraints.rule: stdlib only; no new third-party imports
the existing WebhookDispatcher (app/webhooks.py) must be reused as the dispatch seam — no new HTTP client, worker, or queue introduced
the stage-1 frozen suite tests/test_api.py must pass unmodified; the stage-1 out-of-scope list remains in force

open_questions.question: Does the product ticket note for last_notified_at in GET /todos constitute the formal C1 contract change request (with sign-off) that C1's unfreeze rule requires? If yes: revise C1 via request_contract_revision and plan the response field as a follow-on stage. If no: keep C1 frozen as-is and close the product request. Recorded as non-blocking: the rest of stage 2 (webhook dispatch + registration) is independent of this decision and can execute while the user decides.
